item.title: Federal Prisons: Improved Reviews of Natural Deaths and Communications with Families Needed
item.description:
What GAO Found
The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) reported that about 3,000 people died from natural causes while in its custody in fiscal years 2016 through 2025. GAO reviewed death investigation records for the natural deaths in BOP custody in fiscal year 2024. The documents showed that BOP identified health care deficiencies in 45 percent of these deaths, and that some of these deficiencies contributed to the natural deaths. BOP identified deficiencies such as delayed offsite medical appointments, failures to order necessary medical tests, and shortcomings in emergency responses.
After a death in custody, BOP requires staff to notify the decedent’s emergency contacts and next of kin. However, BOP could not confirm how many of these individuals received such notifications because it did not require that staff document (nor require that BOP management monitor) that these notifications took place. To help address this issue, in May 2026, BOP began requiring staff to document attempts to notify next of kin. However, BOP did not require staff to document attempts to notify emergency contacts or require management to monitor notifications. By taking these steps, BOP management can better ensure that emergency contacts and next of kin receive notifications.
BOP policy requires staff to share the circumstances surrounding a death with the emergency contacts and next of kin. However, BOP policy does not define what is meant by circumstances surrounding a death, and as a result, staff do not have a consistent understanding of what information to share during death notifications. In addition, GAO found that staff do not always share this information even when it is immediately available or when it becomes available later. Monitoring whether staff share the circumstances, and better defining circumstances surrounding a death for staff, would reduce the risk that families will not receive this consequential information from BOP.
BOP policy requires staff to investigate every death that occurs in BOP facilities, excluding legal executions. However, GAO found that BOP does not record all recommendations resulting from these investigations or whether a facility has implemented them. Doing so would give BOP a more complete picture of deficiencies in its health care delivery and enhance its ability to analyze and address deficiencies, while potentially reducing the government’s liabilities.
GAO Findings from Bureau of Prisons (BOP) Investigations of Natural Deaths in Custody
Why GAO Did This Study
Federal law enforcement agencies reported that nearly 4,000 people died in their custody in fiscal years 2016 through 2023. Most of these deaths were reported by BOP (85 percent). BOP is responsible for the care and custody of about 155,000 incarcerated people.
GAO was asked to review BOP’s efforts to investigate natural deaths in custody and notify families of these deaths. This report examines what BOP data show about people who died in BOP custody (i.e., in its facilities) from natural causes in fiscal years 2016 through 2025; what deficiencies in care BOP identified that contributed to natural deaths; the extent to which BOP ensures facilities notify families consistently and in a timely manner; and the extent to which BOP investigated natural deaths in its custody.
GAO reviewed BOP policies and documents, and BOP data on deaths in custody. In addition, GAO selected three BOP facilities and interviewed their leadership and staff. GAO selected locations based on variation in the type of facility (penitentiaries versus medical centers) and number of natural deaths. GAO also interviewed BOP headquarters officials responsible for overseeing death investigations and family notifications.
